notes:
Documentaries and geography explainers can now write and speak narration for visual-only scenes. The local narrator reads above quiet scene audio with timed captions. Scripts with supplied speaking parts retain their words. Requests for ambient sound only remain supported.

Illustrated maps move between a regional overview and closer shoreline views. Great Lakes maps visit individual lakes, and the glacial cross-section shows the ground moving as the ice recedes.

The documentary writer reuses its local model across scenes and removes speaker labels from generated narration.
